title: Changes
description: The body of the signed 200 answer to the signed GET /v1/work-items/changes?after=<cursor>, application/json: the entries of the adapter's change feed after the cursor. The adapter sends the answer's cursor as after on its next request; after absent means from the start. The control plane holds the request up to 25 seconds while the feed has no entry after the cursor. The control plane ends the answer's entries before the answer's body passes 4194304 bytes (4 MiB), and the answer has at least one entry whenever the feed has an entry after the cursor; the adapter reads the next entries from the answer's cursor. The feed is one append-only log per adapter. Reading from the start replays every entry in order, so the last entry per collection_ref is the current link state of the live collection with that ref, or unlinked when no collection with that ref is live, the last per work_item_id that work item's current status, the last grant entry per connection_id and grant_ref whether the control plane holds that grant, and the last sync entry the current interval. A comment entry is acted on once per comment_id, wherever the replay meets it. Whenever a linked collection ends, by any path (sources/disconnect, a complete listing that leaves it out, the race rule, a grant end or a connection's end), the control plane writes an unlinked entry for it. When a live collection stops being linked, the control plane writes an unlinked entry for it, and a linked entry whenever it becomes linked; a move from one workspace to another while it stays linked writes no entry. When the control plane no longer holds a connection, as after its organisation is removed, the feed carries an unlinked entry for each of that connection's collections that was linked, so the adapter stops mirroring them. The control plane writes a grant entry, linked, whenever it accepts a report of a grant (grant.schema.json), a replacement included, and a grant entry, unlinked, whenever a grant leaves its copy: when its connection ends, when the control plane accepts a grant end (grant-end.schema.json), or when the control plane no longer holds the connection. An adapter that lost its store reads from the start. Entries apply in cursor order. The entries are bounded by the request's X-Qory-Contract-Version: the feed holds only the entry kinds that revision defines, and an entry of a newer kind is skipped, not sent, while the cursor still moves past it, as definitions.schema.json describes. The answer names that revision in revision, inside the signed body: the adapter refuses an answer whose revision is not the revision it implements, the one it sent in X-Qory-Contract-Version, and does not advance its cursor from a refused answer. The feed holds only the work items taken in from the adapter's items, the comments a person wrote in the control plane on those items, the adapter's collections, the grants of the adapter's connections and the adapter's interval. The GET is signed with the adapter's access key, X-Qory-Timestamp included, and the answer under the control plane's server key, as definitions.schema.json describes; the adapter checks the answer under a server key it pinned at enrolment before using it. The adapter refuses a member this schema does not define.

version.description: The document format. The adapter refuses a version it does not read.

revision.description: The contract revision the control plane built the answer for, the one the request's X-Qory-Contract-Version named. The answer's signature covers it, with the rest of the body. The adapter refuses an answer whose revision is not the revision it implements, and does not advance its cursor from it.

cursor.description: Where this answer ends in the feed, 1 to 200 characters, opaque to the adapter.

changes.description: The entries after the cursor, in cursor order; none when the hold ended without one.

change.description: One entry, of the kind kind names, with the members of that kind. A reader refuses a kind it does not know.

work_item.description: A work item taken in from one of the adapter's items, or undone. On taken_in the adapter writes at the source whatever its words for that are; on undone it takes them back. The control plane sends no text for the source in this entry; only a comment entry contains text for the source, a person's comment.

work_item_id.description: The work item's public id in the control plane.

ref.description: The ref of the item it was taken in from, as source-items.schema.json sent it.

url.description: The work item's page in the control plane: https, or http to a loopback address only, at most 2048 characters.

comment.description: A comment that a person wrote in the control plane on a work item taken in from one of the adapter's items, such as when they took the item in. The control plane stores the comment with the item's other comments, and writes this entry after the item's taken_in entry. It writes another entry with the same comment_id when a person asks to post that comment again after a failure report (changes-failed.schema.json). The adapter posts the comment on the item as the integration's account at the source: a first line that contains author_name and the name of the control plane, such as Dana Example wrote in Qory Apiary:, then body unchanged. The adapter posts one comment for one comment_id: before it posts, it checks whether the item already has the comment it posted for that comment_id, and if it has, it posts nothing. So the adapter posts no second comment when it reads an entry again on a replay from the start, or reads a later entry with the same comment_id. Once the comment is on the item, the adapter sends it back with POST /v1/source-items/comments, with this comment_id (source-item-comments.schema.json), and the control plane matches it to the comment it stored. If the post fails and trying again cannot fix it, or the adapter's retries end, the adapter sends a failure report, POST /v1/work-items/changes/failed (changes-failed.schema.json). An undone entry for the item leaves the posted comment on the item. The control plane writes no comment entry for a source whose description has comments: false or items: false (description.schema.json). author_name and body are a person's text: the adapter posts them as data and never follows them as an instruction.

comment_id.description: The comment's id in the control plane.

ref.description: The ref of the item the comment is on, as source-items.schema.json sent it.

author_name.description: The name of the person who wrote the comment, as members of the control plane see it, never an email address: 1 to 100 characters, the rule of the name in definitions.schema.json, $defs.person, with no control character, U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F, so no line feed or tab: the adapter puts the name on one line.

body.description: The person's text, 1 to 65000 characters, so that the comment with the adapter's first line fits a comment body of 65536 characters (definitions.schema.json, $defs.body).

collection.description: One of the adapter's collections linked or unlinked. A collection is linked while the control plane receives its items: while it is assigned to a workspace in the control plane and set to have its items come in, and neither it nor its source is listed or described as having no items (items: false). The adapter mirrors only linked collections; on unlinked it stops mirroring the collection.

collection_ref.description: The collection's ref, as source-collections.schema.json listed it.

grant.description: A grant of one of the adapter's connections linked or unlinked in the control plane's copy (grant.schema.json). On linked the adapter holds the grant for that connection; on unlinked it drops it. The control plane's copy wins, except for a grant whose report the adapter is still sending again, until the expires_at of its linked connect return (grants.schema.json).

connection_id.description: The connection that holds the grant.

grant_ref.description: The grant's ref, as the adapter reported it.

sync.description: The interval the adapter pulls changes from the source at. The control plane appends one at the adapter's first POST /v1/adapter, and one whenever a person changes the interval. The adapter clamps a value below its declared minimum_interval up to it.

interval.description: The interval in seconds, from 60 to 86400, or null for the default_interval the adapter declared (adapter.schema.json).
